name: GCSE Business (AQA 8132)
material_vintage: AQA GCSE Business (8132) specification, for first teaching from September 2017, linked from aqa.org.uk/8132 and itemised on 2026-09-27: all six topics across the two papers -- Paper 1 'Influences of operations and HRM on business activity' (Topic 3.1 Business in the real world; Topic 3.2 Influences on business; Topic 3.3 Business operations; Topic 3.4 Human resources) and Paper 2 'Influences of marketing and finance on business activity' (Topic 3.1 Business in the real world, re-examined through a marketing/finance lens; Topic 3.5 Marketing; Topic 3.6 Finance), plus the quantitative skills requirement running through both papers (at least 10% of total marks). Assessment: two linear written papers, each 1 hour 45 minutes, 90 marks, 50% of the GCSE -- each paper has Section A (multiple-choice and short-answer questions, 20 marks), Section B (a case study/data-response set, around 34 marks) and Section C (a further case study/data-response set, around 36 marks), assessing AO1 knowledge/understanding (35%), AO2 application (35%) and AO3 analysis/evaluation (30%) across both papers. Stage tests and the mock are original questions in AQA's style, never real past-paper items; every numerical worked example (break-even, cash-flow forecasts, gross/net profit margin, average rate of return) was computed and verified when this course was built.
level_source: RQF Level 2 (GCSE, grades 1-9), per Ofqual's Register of Regulated Qualifications listing for this specification

learner_notices.text: AQA GCSE Business is heavily case-study/data-response based -- Sections B and C of both papers give the learner a business scenario (often with data, e.g. a small table or a cash-flow extract) and ask questions that apply the topic content to it. Practice always means applying a concept to a specific scenario, not just stating the definition.

At least 10% of all marks across both papers are for quantitative skills. AQA does not give formulae in the exam for gross/net profit margin or average rate of return, so these must be known by heart; break-even is tested by reading a given chart, not by using the break-even formula or drawing a chart from scratch. Always show full working -- AQA awards method marks that a bare correct answer alone will not earn.

AQA explicitly does not examine named motivational theories (e.g. Maslow, Herzberg, Taylor) -- only financial and non-financial motivation methods in general terms. This course does not teach or test theorist names for that reason.
